description: We are a group of friends from Kerala who wanted to know how astronauts survive in space and how we can make life there healthier and safer. Our curiosity led us to choose the theme creating a health monitoring system for astronauts. After all, what’s more chaotic than a bunch of teenagers? The cosmos!
summary:
ASTROVITALS is a software-based astronaut health-monitoring prototype developed by our team, Chaotic Cosmos, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. With the guidance and encouragement of Jiya CS, we worked together to turn our idea into an interactive PictoBlox project.

Our prototype focuses on six important health parameters: heart rate, blood oxygen, body temperature, blood pressure, hydration and sleep hours. Users enter an astronaut's name and manually provide the readings. The system checks them against programmed reference ranges and displays an overall status: NORMAL or CHECK REQUIRED. An astronaut character guides the user through the process.

We wanted to explore how technology could make health monitoring simpler and more organised for astronauts. Although our current version uses manually entered readings rather than live sensors, it represents our first step towards a more advanced system. This project has been a journey of teamwork, learning, problem-solving and turning curiosity into something we could actually build.
details:
What did we develop?

We developed ASTROVITALS, an interactive astronaut health-monitoring prototype using PictoBlox. Our aim was to create a simple system that brings important health readings together in one place.

How does it work?

The user starts the programme and enters the astronaut's name. An astronaut character welcomes the user and guides them to the dashboard. The user then enters six health readings: heart rate, blood oxygen, body temperature, blood pressure, hydration and sleep hours.

Using conditional statements, the programme compares the entered values with its programmed reference ranges. It then displays an overall system status: NORMAL or CHECK REQUIRED. A scan counter also keeps track of monitoring sessions.

Benefits and intended impact

We wanted to make health monitoring easier to understand and organise. By bringing six parameters into one interface, ASTROVITALS demonstrates how a simple software system can help identify readings that fall outside selected reference ranges.

We hope our idea encourages further exploration of technology for astronaut health and well-being.

Tools and technology

We used PictoBlox and its block-based programming environment. Our project uses variables, conditional statements, user inputs, broadcasts, sprites and backdrops to create an interactive experience.

The current version is a software prototype. It does not use physical sensors or collect live medical readings.

Creativity and team contribution

We brought together different ideas and worked towards creating one common project. From planning the interface and deciding what parameters to include to developing the programming logic and testing the prototype, each stage taught us something new.

We faced challenges along the way, especially while bringing our ideas together and making the different parts work as one system. Jiya CS supported us with guidance, suggestions and encouragement throughout this journey. Her support helped us approach the challenge with more confidence and keep improving our work.

Potential considerations

We understand that manually entered readings may not always be accurate. Health reference ranges can also differ depending on the individual and mission conditions. A real-world system would need reliable sensors, secure data handling, expert-reviewed medical standards and professional oversight.

Future scope

In the future, ASTROVITALS could be developed further by integrating actual sensors, collecting readings automatically, securely storing health information and displaying changes over time. These are ideas for future development, not features of our current prototype.
